More generally, every summable real sequence of total mass zero has l1 norm at least twice any one of its coefficients. Applying this to the second Poisson difference and its positive mass exp(-lambda) at zero proves the stronger lower bound. The Lean result also includes lambda=0 for the signed-difference definition.

The sharper bound holds in the full finite rank-one formulation and uniformly throughout every fixed critical band.

findings.original_assumption: Lemma 3.5 is stated for good edges in the leading channels: compatible dependent regular pairs, with private prime coordinates on their distinct normalized values. It gives a rank lower bound with O(1), a width O(B) and B^{O(1)} endpoint patterns.
findings.finding: Finite compression holds for arbitrary positive coprime coefficients a<=b as soon as one normalized value is shared and the distinct normalized values have private parity coordinates. Affine compatibility, dependence, physical separation and a prior local-regularity assumption are unnecessary. Private coordinates already imply both local ranks equal L. The actual compressed rank is |U|-1 and at least (2-1/b)*L-1. There are at most (L+1)^2 fixed integer motifs, all in [-bL,bL]; one fixed-pattern integer anchor determines both centres. The private-value intersection now has an explicit coefficient classification: space(S) intersect space(T)=space(S intersect T), and even coefficients on the true intersection are linearly equivalent to the actual common class space. Actual normalized units are bijective with the deduplicated intersection values. For positive a,b and centres at least two, even selections of the actual units are therefore linearly equivalent to S_x intersect S_y; its rank and the full pair deficiency both equal (u-1)_+, including zero and one unit. Coprimality, alignment height, separation and affine compatibility are unnecessary for this private-intersection classification. The actual affine character of an even true-window selection is its predecessor coefficient. For even exact-unit coefficients, the paired character is the sign of the sum of the two predecessor parities. Full-support pair relations are explicitly reindexed by nonzero actual common classes. For a private normalized pair with positive length, each marginal is proved to equal p=2^-L, and the actual covariance equals p^2 times the signed nonzero even-unit sum. No joint compatibility, separation, coprimality or alignment height is imposed; probability-zero pairs retain their character cancellations.
findings.proposed_revision: State the finite compression for positive coprime coefficients a<=b, a shared normalized value and private coordinates, and then specialize to good edges. Replace the unspecified finite losses and offset count by rank >=(2-1/b)*L-1 and at most (L+1)^2 motifs in [-bL,bL]. State explicitly that the anchor determines both centres and that local regularity follows from the private-coordinate condition. State the exact private-intersection coefficient equivalence and rank identities separately, including zero and one exact unit. Keep the shared-value premise for the full union-compression image identity; the zero-unit intersection result does not remove that premise. Give the actual predecessor characters and private pair covariance with separately chosen local affine witnesses; retain probability-zero pairs and require distinct centres for the two-element event.
findings.impact: Gives explicit finite compression constants, motifs and anchor uniqueness, derives local regularity from privacy, and classifies actual private common classes by even exact-unit coefficients including zero and one unit. Actual predecessor characters and private pair covariance are proved without joint compatibility, separation, coprimality or height restrictions. Full union-image compression still requires a shared value. The subsequent MATH-0045 completes the actual fixed-channel mass T2.5. The complete main pair profile and optimality remain separate unfinished claims.
